newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- FEB 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--A rift has appeared in the teachers' strike, with primary school teachers deciding to end their protests and return to the classrooms with high school teachers vowing to continue for a sixth week.

--Thirty conservative opposition New Democracy deputies support the candidacy of Costas Karamanlis, the nephew and namesake of party founder and former prime minister and president Constantine Karamanlis, to lead the party. Karamanlis's name has been put forward as a "unity" alternative to the other two candidates, incumbent Miltiades Evert and former minister George Souflias.

--The government's plans to introduce productivity bonuses for civil servants hides political and not structural plans, the Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) said yesterday. The bonus, it said, will provoke demands that it be applied to all civil servants and to the private sector and will overturn incomes policy.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou yesterday adopted the opposition's slogan of "a lost decade" for the mistakes in economic policy exercised by ruling party PASOK during the 80s.
--The Karamanlis candidacy for ND leader will cause the most problems for current president Miltiades Evert, sources say, draining him of vital support.
--Investigations into the car bomb targeted at the family of a senior police officer are delving into old cases in an effort to find the perpetrators.

--Both taxpayers and tax collectors are mystified by how to complete the new E9 form on real estate: tax bureaux in Athens yesterday held a briefing seminar for 1,000 employees on how to fill in the E9.
--US Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is preparing a visit to Athens and Nicosia to prepare a US initiative on resolving the Cyprus issue.
--ND leader Miltiades Evert is adamant that he will stand for the post of party president, no matter how many others declare candidacies.
--Reports say that ruling party PASOK-aligned union movement PASKE is trying to "buy" civil servants' and bank employees' silence for two years with increases of 7.5 percent.

--Athens mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos yesterday announced plans to turn major streets in central Athens into pedestrian malls, on the approval of the environment, town planning and public works ministry. Free mini-buses will be introduced to reduce air pollution. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
